independent_reference.reason: Spike (preinstalled at /edatools/opensrc/spike/1.1.1-dev) cannot run on this host: missing libboost_regex.so.1.66.0 / libboost_system.so.1.66.0 with no compatible build anywhere on the system. See docs/issues.md ISS-001 and docs/decisions.md D-002.
independent_reference.scope: register-register and register-immediate ALU ops (OP, OP-IMM) and the complete M extension (MUL/MULH/MULHSU/MULHU/DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU), written directly from the RISC-V ISA spec without reading rtl/rv32im_core.sv or any other DUT source.
independent_reference.not_covered_by_reference_model: loads/stores, branches, JAL/JALR, LUI/AUIPC, FENCE, ECALL/EBREAK, error-halt policy -- these are instead covered by directed tests with hand-computed expected results/outcomes (see directed_tests below).

directed_tests.covers: x0 hardwiring, negative-immediate sign extension, ADD/SUB, SLT/SLTU (signed vs unsigned), SLL/SRL/SRA shifts, XOR/OR/AND, untaken and taken branches, JAL/JALR with return-address check
directed_tests.evidence: logs/ (zsim.log via Animas run); MMIO_TX byte=1 then ERR_HALT cause=7 (EBREAK, the intentional clean-stop convention)
directed_tests.bug_found_and_fixed: RTL bug: ALU SRA used an erroneous `logic'(...)` cast that truncated the signed shift result to 1 bit before zero-extending back to 32 bits (bare `logic` defaults to 1-bit width in SystemVerilog). Found on first run of this test (SRAI(0x80000000,31) produced 1 instead of 0xFFFFFFFF). Fixed in rtl/rv32im_alu.sv; confirmed by rerun. See docs/issues.md.

directed_tests.covers: SB/LB/LBU, SH/LH/LHU sign vs zero extension, SW/LW round-trip, byte- and halfword-level write-strobe isolation (adjacent bytes within a word must not be disturbed)

non-instantaneous memory: req_ready backpressure plus randomized extra response latency, exercising the core's wait-on-ready and wait-on-response paths explicitly (prompt Section 5: 'Do not make execution depend on an instantaneous response')
directed_tests.evidence: Identical pass outcome under altered timing; fetch-of-first-instruction moved from cycle 7 (default +FIXEDLAT=2) to cycle 16, confirming the altered latency was actually exercised, not just accepted as a no-op flag.

directed_tests.covers: MUL, MULH (signed x signed), MULHSU (signed x unsigned), MULHU (unsigned x unsigned), DIV/REM signed, DIVU/REMU unsigned, division by zero (both signed and unsigned), signed overflow (INT_MIN / -1)
illegal instruction (raw word 0xFFFFFFFF, opcode 1111111 is not a legal RV32I/M major opcode)
JALR to a target whose LSB-cleared address is still not 4-byte aligned
a compiled C program: recursion/stack (fib(15) via recursive calls), arrays (sum + bubble sort of an 8-element array), loops, functions
directed_tests.evidence: MMIO_TX byte=1 then ERR_HALT cause=7; ran 110987 cycles on RTL

random_instruction_comparison.scope: register-only ALU + M-extension instruction stream (no loads/stores/branches, so the program is inherently memory-safe and needs no startup code)
random_instruction_comparison.result: PASS -- exact match (pc, instr, rd_we, rd_addr, rd_wdata) for all 1100 retired instructions against scripts/isa_reference_model.py
random_instruction_comparison.evidence: results/random_instruction_comparison.json; build/random_program/ (generated program, reference trace); output/zsim.log (RTL retirement trace) at the time of this run

reset_behavior: Exercised implicitly by every test listed above (each run starts from reset with pc=0 and all registers cleared to 0 by rv32im_regfile's synchronous reset); not tested as a standalone mid-program reset pulse.
not_tested: Mid-execution reset (asserting rst while the core is mid-instruction) -- only power-on/start-of-simulation reset was exercised.
Exhaustive coverage of every immediate value / register combination for every instruction (the random-instruction test samples a large but non-exhaustive space).
Formal verification / model checking of any kind -- all evidence here is simulation-based.
limitations: The independent reference (scripts/isa_reference_model.py) is a second, independently-authored implementation of the ISA, not an externally-maintained, widely-trusted reference such as Spike or Sail (see docs/decisions.md D-002). Directed-test expected values for loads/stores/branches/jumps/errors were computed by hand from the RISC-V ISA specification, not cross-checked against a second automated model.
